cultivar: China, hybrid Assam and Darjeeling clonal mix
processing: Organic Darjeeling orthodox tea from a planting of 51% pure China, 40% hybrid Assam and 9% Darjeeling clonal bushes.
harvest_season: As with other Darjeeling gardens, first flush in early spring and second flush in early summer are the prized pickings; summer clonal lots are also sold.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf, with darker tones in summer lots.
appearance_liquor: Gold to amber by flush, as is typical of Darjeeling.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about the garden's cup. As with other Darjeelings, floral in spring and rounder in summer, with this low-elevation garden's teas sold mainly as clean organic lots.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Summer lots can take a little more time and heat.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, as is usual for Darjeeling, sometimes labelled by bush type (for example a summer clonal black). Best in the first year or two. Output is about 100,000 kg of organic tea a year, so it is not a rarity.
description:
Balasun is an organic garden near Sonada, named for the Balason River that runs past it. It covers about 181 hectares under tea, spread from 365 to 1,375 metres, which is low by Darjeeling standards at the bottom end.

What stands out is its bush mix, more than half pure China with a large share of hybrid Assam. That gives the garden range from flush to flush, and lots may name the bush type.

Little is recorded about a house flavour, so brew it by flush as you would any Darjeeling. Summer clonal lots can take a slightly longer steep.

With around 100,000 kg produced each year, this is an accessible organic Darjeeling. Buying the current year is more important than chasing the name.
history: The garden started in 1871 under Devenport and Company Limited as Nahore Balasun Tea Estate, and later took its name from the river. The Darjeeling Consolidated Tea Company of the Bajoria Group took it over in 1963, and Jay Shree Tea and Industries in 2005.
